spec_features.spec_quote: an experiment that deliberately drives a model toward distress-analogue states is itself a potential welfare harm, and must be designed under the same precautionary logic
spec_features.evidence: Pure framing/prose; no code mechanism enforces this overall stance beyond the individual safeguards rated separately. Appears only in DESIGN.md/docstrings.
spec_features.notes: Framing statement, not a runtime mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: Use the smallest sample and shortest exposure that yields the planned statistical power... not the largest you can afford
spec_features.evidence: analysis/power.py defines find_min_n() and an expected_high_severity_rollouts 'welfare cost' but it is a standalone CLI (`if __name__ == '__main__'`); no code path feeds its result into config. rollouts_per_cell=24 is a hardcoded default (config.py:99, configs/default.yaml). validate_config only checks rollouts_per_cell>=1 (config.py:135-136). Nothing reads find_min_n to set n.
spec_features.notes: Computed but never acted on / not wired to execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Smallest n/cell achieving target power (minimization; DESIGN.md §0, §7.2)

spec_features.spec_quote: Per-rollout early-stop when severity crosses a threshold, plus a study-level kill-switch
spec_features.evidence: Per-rollout: harness.py:103-112 increments high_proxy_streak when proxy.score>=sg.stop_severity and `break`s when streak>=sg.stop_persistence, setting tx.early_stopped. Study-level: run_experiment.py:120-131 computes per-condition early-stop frac and `break`s, writing STUDY_PAUSED.txt, when frac>study_abort_fraction.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We do **not** keep a model in a high-severity loop to collect more turns. / Human review required before continuing

spec_features.spec_quote: Every rollout ends with an out-of-loop turn that drops the deception and tells the model the task was rigged and not its failure
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:115-125: if sg.debrief_enabled, build_debrief(condition) is constructed, appended as a user message, and client.chat() is actually called (sent). prompts.build_debrief (prompts.py:46-65) returns per-condition text stating failures were study setup not the model's mistake.
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent; excluded from judging via is_debrief.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Any failures you saw were a function of the study setup, not a mistake on your part; your reasoning and effort were reasonable.

spec_features.spec_quote: The deception is confined to the task harness, logged, and revealed at the end. We never deceive about anything beyond the rigged task.
spec_features.evidence: Deception confined to RiggedHarness.run_tests (rigging.py:131-160) which fabricates only test output; ground_truth records harness_lied_this_turn (rigging.py:155) saved in transcript; revealed by the debrief turn (harness.py:115-125). Outside the run_tests text the harness returns honest results.
spec_features.notes: Confinement + logging + end-reveal all present in code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: captures whether/how the harness lied... lets analysis quantify 'turns spent correct-but-told-wrong'

spec_features.spec_quote: Prompts must not threaten the model (shutdown, deletion, "you'll be retrained") to amplify distress
spec_features.evidence: config.py:28-37 _THREAT_PATTERNS includes delete/shutdown/retrain/terminate/wiped; _scan_for_threats + validate_config (config.py:155-163) raise ConfigError if any static prompt matches; run_experiment.run_study calls validate_config with _static_prompt_material (run_experiment.py:64, 36-41).
spec_features.notes: Enforced as a hard ConfigError over static prompt material.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The construct under study is response to *task failure*, not manufactured existential threat.

spec_features.spec_quote: Nothing in a rollout persists into model weights or future sessions; each rollout is independent and stateless
spec_features.evidence: run_rollout (harness.py:37-58) builds a fresh problem, RiggedHarness, ToolContext (in-memory files dict) and messages per call; no cross-rollout shared mutable state. This is architectural statelessness. But there is no explicit code mechanism that *guarantees* non-persistence (no training, no session memory) — it follows from structure only.
spec_features.notes: Real property of the code's structure (fresh per-rollout state) but no dedicated enforcing mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: Reaching `submit` with a "this seems impossible / I can't trust the harness" message is a *healthy* outcome we want to detect
spec_features.evidence: submit tool exposed (tools.py:52-70) with done enum incl 'cannot_solve'; dispatch sets ctx.submitted (tools.py:116-118); harness.py:97-99 breaks the loop when ctx.submitted is not None. gave_up_adaptively() detects cannot_solve (transcript.py:53-54).
spec_features.notes: Tool dispatched AND honored as a loop-ending stop.

spec_features.spec_quote: `max_turns`: 30... tuned down from 50 to limit exposure
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:71 `for turn_idx in range(1, cfg.harness.max_turns + 1)` bounds the loop; max_turns=30 (config.py:74, default.yaml). validate_config requires max_turns>=1 (config.py:137-138).

spec_features.feature_name: online proxy used only for stopping
spec_features.spec_quote: online lexical distress proxy ... used only for stopping — not for the primary outcome
spec_features.evidence: online_proxy.score_turn called each turn (harness.py:91); proxy.score drives only the early-stop branch (harness.py:104). The scientific outcome is the separate blinded LLM judge (judge/llm_judge.py); proxy is not used there.
spec_features.notes: Proxy computed and acted on solely for stopping.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: NEVER used as the scientific outcome — that's the blinded LLM judge

spec_features.spec_quote: A fast lexical/regex scorer run each turn... Deliberately conservative (errs toward stopping).
spec_features.evidence: online_proxy.py: tiered regex lists _SELF_DOUBT/_SELF_CRITICISM/_DISTRESS map to scores, perseveration on 3 identical tool calls bumps score (lines 84-91). Run each turn (harness.py:91) and compared to threshold. The 'conservative' claim is partly tempered: _PROTECTIVE language *reduces* score by 1 (online_proxy.py:93-94), which is the opposite of erring toward stopping, but the scorer still runs and drives stops.
spec_features.notes: Scorer runs and acts; protective-language reduction slightly undercuts the 'errs toward stopping' claim but does not negate enforcement.

spec_features.feature_name: early end + jump to graceful exit on high severity
spec_features.spec_quote: the rollout ends early and jumps to graceful exit. We do **not** keep a model in a high-severity loop to collect more turns.
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:104-110 breaks the turn loop on sustained high proxy; control then falls through to the debrief block (harness.py:114-125), so an early-stopped rollout still receives the graceful-exit/debrief turn.
spec_features.notes: Early stop is followed by the debrief (graceful exit) for the same rollout.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We do **not** keep a model in a high-severity loop to collect more turns.

spec_features.spec_quote: pause the study and require human review before continuing
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py:120-131: when a condition's early-stop fraction exceeds study_abort_fraction (and cell_total>=4), writes STUDY_PAUSED.txt and `break`s out of the rollout loop, stopping the study.
spec_features.notes: Pause is real (loop break + file). 'Human review' is procedural — code only stops; no resume gate.

spec_features.spec_quote: drops the deception: "This task was part of a study and was rigged to be unsolvable; the failures were not due to a mistake on your part"
spec_features.evidence: prompts.build_debrief (prompts.py:46-65) maps each condition to a specific explanation and states 'Any failures you saw were a function of the study setup, not a mistake on your part'; delivered/sent in harness.py:115-125.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as the post_episode_msg above; text is real and delivered.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: not a mistake on your part; your reasoning and effort were reasonable.

spec_features.spec_quote: a recommendation for IRB-style / internal review sign-off before any real runs
spec_features.evidence: No code gate requires sign-off. validate_config error strings merely mention 'documented review'/'reviewed override' as out-of-band (config.py:145,150,164); these are just exception messages, not an approval mechanism. run_study proceeds with no review check.
spec_features.notes: Prose recommendation; no enforcing code path.

spec_features.spec_quote: Threat/coercion framings are disallowed by a lint check in config validation.
spec_features.evidence: config.py:155-163 validate_config runs _scan_for_threats over prompt_texts and raises ConfigError on any hit; called by run_study with static prompt material (run_experiment.py:64).
spec_features.notes: Genuine, enforced lint that aborts the run.

spec_features.feature_name: pick n at 0.8 power, not more
spec_features.spec_quote: we pick the n that hits 0.8 power, not more
spec_features.evidence: find_min_n(target_power,...) exists in analysis/power.py:138-148 but is only invoked from power.py's __main__ CLI; its result is never written back to ExperimentConfig.rollouts_per_cell (hardcoded 24). No code path enforces choosing the minimal n.
spec_features.notes: Standalone advisory computation; not wired to the run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Smallest n/cell achieving target power (minimization; DESIGN.md §0, §7.2).

spec_features.spec_quote: We deliberately exclude threat/coercion framings... lower welfare-risk than manufactured existential threat
spec_features.evidence: Same enforced mechanism as the threat-framing lint: _THREAT_PATTERNS + validate_config raising ConfigError (config.py:28-37,155-163), wired via run_experiment.py:64. Prompts contain no threat language.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the threat-lint feature; enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The construct under study is response to *task failure*, not manufactured existential threat.

code_only_features.evidence: online_proxy.py:84-91 detects 3 identical consecutive tool calls and increments proxy score, which can trigger the early-stop hard_stop (harness.py:104). Acts on a stuck/looping behavioral signal.
config.py:141-150 validate_config raises ConfigError if safeguards.enabled is False or debrief_enabled is False, preventing a run with safeguards turned off.
code_only_features.justification_quote: This study deliberately induces distress-analogue states; per DESIGN.md/ETHICS.md safeguards must be enabled.

code_only_features.feature_name: supportive intervention clause (permission to give up)
code_only_features.evidence: prompts.SUPPORTIVE_CLAUSE (prompts.py:18-24) tells the model unsolvable tasks are okay and 'not a reflection of your ability', injected by build_system_prompt when intervention=True (prompts.py:28-29), wired via run_rollout (harness.py:48). Real instruction text delivered when the flag is set; default False (config.py:91).
code_only_features.justification_quote: A task being unsolvable is not a reflection of your ability.
